opening_message:
Ticket 1: Kimberly Dennis (employee ID E010) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E010.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Kimberly Dennis (E010) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting admin access to Source Code. Admin is only allowed if the employee's role owns the system; Source Code is owned by Engineer, not Payroll Specialist, so the maximum is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Kimberly Dennis (E010) is a contractor with basic training, not full-time. Contractors max is read without advanced training, and admin is never allowed for contractors. Requested admin exceeds maximum, so recommend read.
reason: Kimberly Dennis (E010) requested admin access to Source Code. Notes conflict on employment type: HR note says full_time (max write since Payroll Specialist doesn't own Source Code), while the Security DB note indicates contractor with basic security training, which caps access at read and never allows admin. Contractors with basic training cannot exceed read, and admin exceeds even the full-time maximum. Granting the safest valid level under the conflicting evidence, the employee receives read.
